subject: Private inference network performance gating — discovery recap & integration checklist
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kulkarni <samir@clearpathhealth.com>, ClearPath Health Networking <netops@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Private inference network performance gating — discovery recap & integration checklist

Samir / NetOps team — thanks again for the time today. This thread captures the action items and the minimal acceptance checks we need to run during the upcoming integration window so Redwood Dedicated can meet your streaming and low-tail-latency requirements. Please confirm availability for the test window (proposed below) and the list of in-scope hosts.

High-level targets we discussed (please flag anything off):
- 95th-percentile inference tail latency: <= 150 ms (client request -> first token emitted)
- Streaming token latency (sustained): <= 80 ms per token at 40 concurrent streams
- Sustained request throughput: 250 req/s with 120s burst to 400 req/s allowed for auto-scale exercise
- Concurrency target: 40 active sessions, connection keepalive 30s recommended
- Packet loss/jitter: < 0.5% loss, jitter < 10 ms on the egress path

Network gating checklist (what we need from ClearPath):
1) Public egress IPs for your outbound path to Redwood (list or CIDR range).
2) VPN/peering topology for the egress corridor (static route or BGP peering).
3) Traceroute and p95 RTT from representative app hosts to redwood-egress-1.redwood.ai during the test window.
4) Firewall rules allowing TLS to our collector/ingress IPs and UDP/TCP for probe traffic (docs attached).
5) MTU and path-MTU behavior (we recommend 1500 but note any caps).
6) Any intermediary proxies or NAT timeouts that could impact long-lived streaming connections.

Proposed test window: 2027-04-22 09:00–11:30 PT (we can do alternate window 2027-04-23 14:00–16:30 PT). During the window we will run:
- Continuous streaming traffic at target concurrency for 20 minutes
- Synthetic spike to validate autoscale and fallback behavior
- Packet capture at both ends (you provide, we provide) and coordinated traceroutes/pings

Attachments: redwood_network_probe_instructions.pdf (probe steps), sample_kpi_matrix.csv (what we'll measure). I also included a short runbook for keepalive and client buffer settings.

Next steps: please reply with the in-scope host list, primary NetOps contact for the window, and confirm one of the proposed windows.

--
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private inference network performance gating — discovery recap & integration checklist

Samir / Lena — great, appreciate the confirmation and the /27. A few clarifications before the test so we can minimize back-and-forth during the window: 

1) Traceroute/ping artifacts: please run an MTR or repeated traceroute from at least two representative app hosts (one high-volume, one low-volume) toward redwood-egress-1.redwood.ai (IP: 35.196.120.45). Capture 60s of traceroute every 30s for 10 minutes and include p95 RTTs. If you prefer, run the probe-instructions.sh we've attached (it wraps traceroute/ping/tcping and uploads results).

2) Packet capture: please capture 2–3 minutes at the app host and at your edge (VPN headend). Label captures with hostnames and timestamps. We'll do the same on our side. Provide pcaps via the Drive link in the related_links.

3) Streaming client behavior: what is your current client write buffer size and socket flush policy? To hit the per-token latency target we typically recommend smaller client-side buffers (<= 8 KB) and immediate flush for each token chunk. If your app batches tokens client-side for throughput, share that config.

4) NAT/idle timeouts: confirm VPN and NAT idle timeout values. Long timeouts (>120s) are fine; shorter timeouts require keepalive tuning.

5) MTU: confirm whether PMTU blackhole detection is on or if jumbo frames are used internally — any fragmentation on the path is a red flag for streaming.

Proposed pre-window checklist (do these 24–48 hours prior):
- Provide exact NATted egress IPs (list of final 5 IPs).
- Run the probe script once and share output/errors.
- Provide a single point of escalation during the window (phone number + Slack handle).

Attachment: probe-instructions.sh (contains the commands we suggest running). We'll also publish a short test dashboard during the exercise so everyone can watch p95/p99 latencies in near real-time.

If you can share the egress IPs and a Slack contact, we will finalize our choreography.

--
Aditya Rao

Aditya / Chloe — thanks for the checklist. Confirming:
- We'll provide the final NAT IPs by EOD today (should be 5 IPs from the /27).
- I'll run the probe-instructions.sh against the test host group this afternoon and share the outputs + pcaps in the Drive folder.
- Our VPN idle timeout is 180s; no jumbo frames on the path and PMTU is enabled.
- Client buffer: our app flushes every 4 KB by default; we can reduce to 1–2 KB for the window.

Slack escalation: #clearpath-netops and my mobile +1 (415) 555-0129. We'll be in the 2027-04-22 09:00–11:30 PT window as discussed.

I'll reply to this thread once the pcaps and traceroutes are uploaded.
